> **What this case shows** — detrending is the quiet first step of almost every spectral analysis:
> remove the slow drift before you estimate the spectrum, or the trend **leaks** spurious
> low-frequency power. `detrendSignal` runs before the [Welch](../eeg-bandpower-welch-eegmmidb/index.qmd)
> and [spectrogram](../eeg-spectrogram-scipy-eegmmidb/index.qmd) estimates — but had never been
> checked against the reference. Here it is certified: on a real drifting frontopolar channel (Fpz)
> it reproduces `scipy.signal.detrend` **bit-for-bit** (max |diff| ~**1e-12** for linear, exactly
> **0** for constant). And the finding is a real methodological point: the **linear** detrend removes
> a low-frequency trend that **constant** (mean) removal leaves in — sub-1-Hz power falls from
> **1284** (raw) to **59** after linear but only to **112** after constant, so the detrend *type*
> removes ~**47%** more low-frequency leakage.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — before any spectral or fluctuation analysis: `detrendSignal(pe, type = "linear")` to
strip the drift.
**Way of thinking** — a trend is not noise you can ignore: it spills energy across the low
frequencies of the spectrum (spectral leakage). *Constant* detrend (mean removal) does nothing about
a slope; *linear* detrend removes it. Match the detrend to the drift.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioPreprocess::detrendSignal()`; `type = "linear"` (least-squares line) or
`"constant"` (mean).
:::

## Proposition

On real drifting Fpz EEG, `detrendSignal` reproduces `scipy.signal.detrend` bit-for-bit (max |diff|
~1e-12 linear, 0 constant); and linear detrend leaves far less sub-1-Hz power (59) than constant
(112), a ~47% reduction.

## Question & goal

**The question is fidelity and consequence: does the ecosystem's detrend equal
`scipy.signal.detrend` — and does the choice of linear vs constant actually change the spectrum?**
The goal is a machine-precision certification of the primitive and a demonstration of why its type
matters.

## Challenge & approach

`detrendSignal("linear")` subtracts the least-squares line (`stats::lm.fit`); `"constant"` subtracts
the mean — exactly `scipy.signal.detrend(type = "linear"/"constant")`. We re-compute both with scipy
(bit-exact), and quantify the consequence with Welch's method: the sub-1-Hz power of the raw signal
and of each detrend.

```
Fpz EEG (eegmmidb, 160 Hz) → detrendSignal(linear / constant) → detrended signal
                    vs scipy.signal.detrend                      → bit-exact (1e-12 / 0)
                    sub-1-Hz Welch power: raw 1284 → linear 59, constant 112 → type matters (−47%)
```

## Data

**EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb, PhysioNet)**: subject **S002**, run **R02
(eyes-closed)**, channel **Fpz** (frontopolar — the largest linear drift of the montage), 10 s at
160 Hz — subset from the same git-tracked root the
[Welch](../eeg-bandpower-welch-eegmmidb/index.qmd),
[spectrogram](../eeg-spectrogram-scipy-eegmmidb/index.qmd), and
[coherence](../eeg-coherence-scipy-eegmmidb/index.qmd) cases use. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: the raw Fpz signal (grey) with its least-squares trend (red — detrendSignal equals scipy exactly) and the linear-detrended signal (blue). Right: the sub-1-Hz Welch power of the raw signal, the constant (mean) detrend, and the linear detrend — the linear detrend cuts ~47% more low-frequency leakage than constant, because it removes the trend that mean-removal leaves in.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* the left panel is the operation (the trend the op removes, = scipy); the right
panel is the consequence (linear detrend removes the trend's low-frequency leakage that constant
detrend leaves behind).

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| op vs `scipy.signal.detrend` (max \|diff\|) | **1e-12** (linear), **0** (constant) |
| linear trend removed | **0.014** µV/sample |
| sub-1-Hz power — raw | **1284** |
| sub-1-Hz power — **linear** detrend | **59** |
| sub-1-Hz power — **constant** detrend | **112** |
| **extra leakage removed (linear vs constant)** | **47%** |

The op equals scipy to the floating-point floor, and the detrend type visibly changes the
low-frequency spectrum. Values trace to
[`artifacts/detrend_summary.csv`](artifacts/detrend_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

The ecosystem's detrend *is* `scipy.signal.detrend` — bit-for-bit, because the least-squares-line and
mean formulas are identical — so the primitive that underlies the Welch and spectrogram estimates is
certified against the reference; and on real drifting EEG the choice of linear vs constant detrend
changes the sub-1-Hz spectrum by ~47%. The transferable takeaway: **detrend before you estimate a
spectrum, and match the detrend to the drift — a slope needs *linear* detrend, because *constant*
(mean) removal leaves the trend's low-frequency leakage in; and remember that linear detrend removes
only the linear part, so oscillatory wander still needs a high-pass filter.**

## Open questions

- Linear detrend removes only the **linear** trend; real EEG baseline wander is oscillatory
  (sub-1-Hz), which a high-pass or smoothness-priors detrend removes more completely. Comparing
  linear detrend, a 0.5-Hz high-pass, and a smoothness-priors detrend on the same channel — and their
  effect on the downstream alpha-power estimate — would show how much residual wander still biases the
  spectrum. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| linear / constant detrend | `detrendSignal()` | PhysioPreprocess |
| the spectrum it precedes | `bandPower(method = "welch")` | PhysioAnalysis |
| the time-frequency view | `spectrogram()` | PhysioAnalysis |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **type** — `"linear"` (subtract the least-squares line; use when there's a slope/drift) vs
  `"constant"` (subtract the mean; use only when there's an offset but no slope).
- **when it's not enough** — linear detrend removes a straight-line trend; for oscillatory baseline
  wander, follow with a high-pass filter (or use a polynomial/spline detrend).
- **why it matters** — a residual trend leaks into the low-frequency bins of every spectrum; detrend
  first, especially for delta-band or fluctuation (DFA) analyses.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioPreprocess)

pe_dt <- detrendSignal(pe, type = "linear")   # strip the drift before the spectrum
# assay(pe_dt, "detrended")

# equals scipy.signal.detrend bit-for-bit (max |diff| ~1e-12 linear, 0 constant);
# linear detrend removes ~47% more sub-1-Hz power than constant on a drifting channel.
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/detrend_summary.csv`](artifacts/detrend_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks
each number, the bit-exact scipy match (linear + constant), the linear-vs-constant leakage reduction,
its internal consistency, and the honestly-noted methodological (not physiological) scope.
